title: Three hundred, five hundred
goal: Buy headphones from a shop assistant in an electronics shop: ask prices in the hundreds, compare them and pay
tip: For the hundreds, put the short number before miya: thalāth miya 300, arbaʿ miya 400, khams miya 500, tisʿ miya 900 (200 is mītēn). Add the tens with w: thalāth miya w khamsīn 350. A dirham has a hundred fils, so khamsīn fils is half a dirham.
grammar: hundreds: number + miya (thalāth miya … tisʿ miya); dirham and fils
dialogue: B
مساء الخير. أبي سماعات حق الدراسة
masāʼ il-khēr. abi sammāʿāt ḥagg id-dirāsa
Good evening. I want some headphones for studying.
A
مساء النور. هذي زينة، بتسع مية
masāʼ in-nūr. hādhi zēna, b-tisʿ miya
Good evening. These are good. They're nine hundred.
B
تسع مية؟ غالية وايد! عندك سماعات أرخص؟
tisʿ miya? ghālya wāyid! ʿindak sammāʿāt arkhaṣ?
Nine hundred? That's really expensive! Have you got cheaper headphones?
A
هذيك بخمس مية، وهذيك بثلاث مية وخمسين
hādhīch b-khams miya, w hādhīch b-thalāth miya w khamsīn
Those are five hundred, and those are three hundred and fifty.
B
زين، باخذ اللي بثلاث مية وخمسين
zēn, bākhidh illi b-thalāth miya w khamsīn
OK, I'll take the ones for three hundred and fifty.
A
ثلاث مية وخمسين درهم. كاش ولا بطاقة؟
thalāth miya w khamsīn dirham. kāsh walla biṭāga?
Three hundred and fifty dirhams. Cash or card?
B
كاش. هذي أربع مية. وقبل لا أنسى، الفاتورة!
kāsh. hādhi arbaʿ miya. w gabil la ansa, il-fātūra!
Cash. Here's four hundred. And before I forget, the receipt!
items: 600 sitt miya, 700 sabʿ miya, 800 thamān miya
the hundreds first, then the tens with w: mītēn w ʿishrīn = 220
a dirham has a hundred fils (فلس); Kuwait: dīnār (دينار)
expensive (with a feminine word, or several things)

title: Fifty thousand for a car
goal: In the office car park, Maryam shows you the car she has bought: ask the price and talk in thousands of dirhams
tip: alf is 1,000 and alfēn 2,000. From 3,000 to 10,000 use ālāf: thalāth ālāf, khams ālāf, ʿashar ālāf. From 11,000 up, alf stays as it is: ʿishrīn alf, khamsīn alf. Add the rest with w: alfēn w khams miya is 2,500.
grammar: thousands: alf, alfēn, thalāth ālāf … ʿashar ālāf; ʿishrīn alf
dialogue: A
شوف سيارتي اليديدة! شرايك؟
shūf sayyārti l-yidīda! shrāyak?
Look at my new car! What do you think?
B
ما شاء الله، حلوة! أكيد غالية. بكم؟
mā shāʼ allāh, ḥilwa! akīd ghālya. b-cham?
Wow, it's lovely! It must have been expensive. How much?
A
بخمسين ألف. مب يديدة، عمرها ثلاث سنين
b-khamsīn alf. mub yidīda, ʿumrha thalāth snīn
Fifty thousand. It's not new, it's three years old.
B
خمسين ألف؟ كل اللي عندي ثلاث آلاف!
khamsīn alf? kill illi ʿindi thalāth ālāf!
Fifty thousand? All I've got is three thousand!
A
بثلاث آلاف؟ تشتري سيكل بس!
b-thalāth ālāf? tishtiri sēkal bas!
With three thousand? You'll only buy a bike!
B
عادي. وتدفعين حق البنك كل شهر؟
ʿādi. w tidfaʿīn ḥagg il-bank kill shahar?
That's fine. And do you pay the bank every month?
A
هيه، ألفين في الشهر، لين سنة ألفين وثلاثين!
hē, alfēn fi sh-shahar, lēn sanat alfēn w thalāthīn!
Yes, two thousand a month, until 2030!
items: the same up to 10,000: arbaʿ ālāf, khams ālāf … ʿashar ālāf (عشرة آلاف)
from 11,000 up alf stays the same: ʿishrīn alf 20,000; miyat alf 100,000
it's three years old (a feminine thing); she's three
a masculine thing or a boy: ʿumrah (عمره)
you buy (to a man); she buys

title: Third street on the right
goal: Find Sēf's new flat: follow his directions on the phone with ordinals (third street, fourth building, tenth floor)
tip: Ordinals: thāni 2nd, thālith 3rd, rābiʿ 4th, khāmis 5th … ʿāshir 10th. Before a noun, with no il-, they mean 'the …': thālith shāriʿ 'the third street', rābiʿ bināya 'the fourth building'. After a noun with il-, they agree like adjectives: iṭ-ṭābig il-ʿāshir 'the tenth floor'.
grammar: ordinals: thāni … ʿāshir before a noun; ākhir wāḥid
dialogue: B
ألو سيف، طلعت من المترو. وين الشقة؟
alō Sēf, ṭilaʿt min il-mitro. wēn ish-shigga?
Hello Sēf, I've come out of the metro. Where's the flat?
A
روح سيدا، وثالث شارع على اليمين
rūḥ sīda, w thālith shāriʿ ʿala l-yamīn
Go straight on, and it's the third street on the right.
B
ثالث شارع؟ زين. وبعدها؟
thālith shāriʿ? zēn. w baʿd-ha?
The third street? OK. And after that?
A
رابع بناية، اللي يم الإشارة. الطابق العاشر
rābiʿ bināya, illi yamm il-ishāra. iṭ-ṭābig il-ʿāshir
The fourth building, the one by the traffic lights. The tenth floor.
B
العاشر؟! في لفت؟
il-ʿāshir?! fī lift?
The tenth?! Is there a lift?
A
هيه. يلا، الكل هني. انت آخر واحد!
hē. yalla, il-kill hni. inta ākhir wāḥid!
Yes. Come on, everyone's here. You're the last one!
B
ياي! لا تاكلون قبل لا أوصل!
yāy! la tāklūn gabil la ōṣal!
I'm coming! Don't eat before I get there!
items: before a noun: thālith shāriʿ = the third street
seventh: sābiʿ; eighth: thāmin; ninth: tāsiʿ
to a woman: inti ākhir waḥda (انتي آخر وحدة)
on the left: ʿala l-yasār (على اليسار)
the floor, the storey (of a building)
to one man: la tākil (لا تاكل)

title: My birthday's in month nine
goal: Ask Sēf when his birthday is and how old he'll be, and say months by their number
tip: The easy way to say a month is shahar + its number: shahar tisʿa 'September', shahar ʿashra 'October'. You'll also hear the month names. Next month is ish-shahar il-yāy, last month ish-shahar illi ṭāf, and ākhir ish-shahar is 'the end of the month'.
grammar: months by number: shahar + number; ish-shahar il-yāy / illi ṭāf
dialogue: B
سيف، قبل لا أنسى، متى عيد ميلادك؟
Sēf, gabil la ansa, mita ʿīd mīlādak?
Sēf, before I forget, when's your birthday?
A
في شهر عشرة، آخر الشهر
fi shahar ʿashra, ākhir ish-shahar
In October, at the end of the month.
B
يعني الشهر الياي! كم عمرك الحين؟
yaʿni ish-shahar il-yāy! cham ʿumrak il-ḥīn?
So next month! How old are you now?
A
ثنين وعشرين، وبيصير عمري ثلاثة وعشرين. وانت؟
thnēn w ʿishrīn, w biyṣīr ʿumri thalātha w ʿishrīn. w inta?
Twenty-two, and I'll be twenty-three. And you?
B
عيد ميلادي كان في شهر تسعة، الشهر اللي طاف
ʿīd mīlādi kān fi shahar tisʿa, ish-shahar illi ṭāf
My birthday was in September, last month.
A
والله؟ ليش ما قلت لي؟
wallāh? lēsh ma gilt-li?
Really? Why didn't you tell me?
B
كنت مسافر ويا أهلي. وصار عمري عشرين!
kint msāfir wiyya ahli. w ṣār ʿumri ʿishrīn!
I was away with my family. And I've turned twenty!
items: the same for every month: shahar ʿashra = October
last week: il-usbūʿ illi ṭāf (الأسبوع اللي طاف)
the start of the month: awwal ish-shahar (أول الشهر)
to a woman: mita ʿīd mīlādich? (متى عيد ميلادج؟)
how old are you? (to a man)
to a woman: cham ʿumrich? (كم عمرج؟)
ṣār ʿumri ʿishrīn = I've turned twenty

title: Checkpoint 2.3: a surprise for Sēf
goal: Plan Sēf's birthday dinner with Fahad and Maryam: say when it is, agree on a place and split the bill
tip: To a group, 'don't' takes -ūn: la tgūlūn-lah 'don't tell him' (to one man: la tgūl-lah). After kill wāḥid 'each person' the verb is the he-form: kill wāḥid yidfaʿ 'each person pays'. ma ʿindi illa means 'I've only got'.
grammar: checkpoint 2.3: recycle s2u037–s2u053 (kān, time clauses, illi, numbers, ordinals, months)
dialogue: B
يا جماعة، عيد ميلاد سيف آخر الشهر
yā jamāʿa, ʿīd mīlād Sēf ākhir ish-shahar
Everyone, Sēf's birthday is at the end of the month.
A
إيه، أدري. شنو نسوي له؟
ēh, adri. shinu nsawwī-lah?
Yes, I know. What shall we do for him?
B
نتعشى في المطعم اللي يم البحر؟
nitʿashsha fi l-maṭʿam illi yamm il-baḥar?
Shall we have dinner at the restaurant by the sea?
A
فكرة حلوة! بس كم بيكون الحساب؟
fikra ḥilwa! bas cham biykūn il-ḥsāb?
Good idea! But how much will the bill be?
B
تقريبا ست مية. كل واحد يدفع ميتين
tagrīban sitt miya. kill wāḥid yidfaʿ mītēn
About six hundred. Each of us pays two hundred.
A
زين، بس ما عندي إلا دنانير!
zēn, bas ma ʿindi illa danānīr!
OK, but I've only got dinars!
B
عادي، بالبطاقة. بس لا تقولون له شي، خلوها مفاجأة!
ʿādi, bil-biṭāga. bas la tgūlūn-lah shay, khallūha mufājaʼa!
No problem, pay by card. But don't tell him anything, you two. Keep it a surprise!
items: kill wāḥid yidfaʿ = each person pays
we do (something) for him; shall we do (something) for him?
Kuwait's money: dīnār (دينار), more than one: danānīr (دنانير)
to one man: la tgūl-lah (لا تقول له); to one woman: la tgūlīn-lah (لا تقولين له)
leave it, keep it (a feminine thing) (to a group)
khallūha mufājaʼa = keep it a surprise; to one man: khallha (خلها)

title: My head hurts
goal: At the office, tell Maryam you're not feeling well, answer her get-well wishes and agree to go home
tip: shfīk? 'what's wrong?' asks a man; to a woman it's shfīch? Say what hurts, then yʿawwirni: rāsi yʿawwirni 'my head hurts'. To someone ill, say salāmāt or ma tshūf shar. The reply to both is allāh ysallmak, or allāh ysallmich to a woman.
grammar: recycle: present and past (yʿawwirni, aḥiss, ma tshūf)
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. شفيك؟ انت تعبان؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. shfīk? inta taʿbān?
Good morning. What's wrong? Are you unwell?
B
صباح النور. هيه، شوي تعبان. راسي يعورني
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. hē, shwayy taʿbān. rāsi yʿawwirni
Good morning. Yes, I'm not feeling great. I've got a headache.
A
سلامات! من متى؟
salāmāt! min mita?
Oh no, get well soon! Since when?
B
الله يسلمج. من البارحة، وأحس بدوخة بعد
allāh ysallmich. min il-bārḥa, w aḥiss b-dōkha baʿad
Thank you. Since last night, and I feel dizzy too.
A
ما تشوف شر. روح البيت وارتاح
ma tshūf shar. rūḥ il-bēt w irtāḥ
I hope it's nothing. Go home and rest.
B
الله يسلمج. بس عندي اجتماع الساعة عشر
allāh ysallmich. bas ʿindi ijtimāʿ is-sāʿa ʿashr
Thank you. But I've got a meeting at ten.
A
عادي، بقول للمدير. والشغل اللي عندك، بسويه أنا
ʿādi, bagūl lil-mudīr. w ish-shughul illi ʿindak, basawwīh ana
That's fine, I'll tell the manager. And the work you've got, I'll do it.
items: what's wrong? what's the matter? (to a man)
to a woman: shfīch? (شفيج؟); UAE also: shu fīk? (شو فيك؟)
tired; unwell, not feeling well (a man)
my head hurts, I've got a headache
say the part that hurts first, then yʿawwirni
oh no, get well soon (to someone ill or hurt)
get well soon, I hope it's nothing (to a man; lit. may you see no harm)
to a woman: ma tshūfīn shar (ما تشوفين شر); reply: allāh ysallmak
God keep you (reply to get-well wishes or thanks, to a woman)
to a man: allāh ysallmak (الله يسلمك)
to a woman: rūḥi l-bēt (روحي البيت)
rest, get some rest (to a man)

title: At the clinic
goal: See a doctor at a clinic: say what hurts, since when and what you ate
tip: khēr? on its own means 'what's up? is everything OK?'. ʿasa ma shar? 'nothing serious, I hope?' is answered ma shar, il-ḥamdu lillāh. Use the past for what happened (kalt simach 'I ate fish') and the present for now (ma agdar ākil 'I can't eat').
grammar: recycle: past for what happened, present for how you feel now
dialogue: A
تفضل اقعد. خير؟ عسى ما شر؟
tfaẓẓal igʿid. khēr? ʿasa ma shar?
Please sit down. What's the matter? Nothing serious, I hope?
B
ما شر، الحمد لله. بس بطني يعورني يا دكتور
ma shar, il-ḥamdu lillāh. bas baṭni yʿawwirni yā daktōr
Nothing serious, thank God. But my stomach hurts, doctor.
A
سلامات! من متى؟ وشو كلت؟
salāmāt! min mita? w shu kalt?
Oh dear! Since when? And what did you eat?
B
الله يسلمك. من يومين، كلت سمك في مطعم يديد
allāh ysallmak. min yōmēn, kalt simach fi maṭʿam yidīd
Thank you. For two days. I ate fish at a new restaurant.
A
يمكن من الأكل. فيك حرارة؟
yimkin min il-akil. fīk ḥarāra?
Maybe it's the food. Have you got a temperature?
B
لا، بس ما أقدر آكل شي
la, bas ma agdar ākil shay
No, but I can't eat anything.
A
بكتب لك دوا، خذه من الصيدلية اللي تحت
baktib-lak dawa, khudhah min iṣ-ṣaydaliyya illi taḥt
I'll write you a prescription. Get it from the pharmacy downstairs.
items: what's up? what's the matter? is everything OK?
said when someone calls or comes to you, or looks worried
reply: ma shar, il-ḥamdu lillāh (ما شر، الحمد لله)
my stomach hurts, I've got a stomach ache
a woman doctor: daktōra (دكتورة); yā daktōr = doctor (talking to him)
for two days (now), since two days ago
fīk ḥarāra? = have you got a temperature? (to a man); to a woman: fīch ḥarāra?
I'll write (it) for you (to a man)

title: Twice a day, after food
goal: Get your medicine from a pharmacist (a woman): how many tablets, when to take them and how much it costs
tip: Numbers come back for medicine: ḥabba waḥda 'one tablet', marratēn fi l-yōm 'twice a day', thalāth marrāt fi l-yōm 'three times a day'. gabil and baʿd work before a noun too: gabil il-akil 'before food', baʿd il-akil 'after food'.
grammar: recycle: present (ākhidh, tishrab) with numbers and gabil / baʿd
dialogue: B
مساء الخير. عندي وصفة من الدكتور
masāʼ il-khēr. ʿindi waṣfa min id-daktōr
Good evening. I've got a prescription from the doctor.
A
مساء النور. سلامتك! تفضل، هذا الدوا
masāʼ in-nūr. salāmtak! tfaẓẓal, hādha d-dawa
Good evening. I hope you feel better! Here's the medicine.
B
الله يسلمج. كم حبة آخذ؟
allāh ysallmich. cham ḥabba ākhidh?
Thank you. How many tablets do I take?
A
حبة وحدة، مرتين في اليوم
ḥabba waḥda, marratēn fi l-yōm
One tablet, twice a day.
B
قبل الأكل ولا بعد الأكل؟
gabil il-akil walla baʿd il-akil?
Before food or after food?
A
بعد الأكل. والدوا بخمسة وأربعين درهم
baʿd il-akil. w id-dawa b-khamsa w arbaʿīn dirham
After food. And the medicine is forty-five dirhams.
B
تفضلي خمسين. مشكورة!
tfaẓẓali khamsīn. mashkūra!
Here's fifty. Thank you!
items: I hope you feel better, get well soon (to a man)
to a woman: salāmtich (سلامتج); reply: allāh ysallmak
three times a day: thalāth marrāt fi l-yōm

title: A small accident
goal: Sēf calls: he's had a small accident. Check he's all right, ask if anyone is hurt and if he has called the ambulance
tip: The past tells what happened: ṣār-li ḥādith 'I've had an accident', tʿawwar 'he got hurt', ittaṣalt 'I called; you called'. ma fīni shay means 'nothing's wrong with me, I'm fine'. salāmtak 'I hope you're OK' works after an accident too.
grammar: recycle: past (ṣār, tʿawwar, ittaṣalt) and present (yʿawwir)
dialogue: A
ألو، وينك؟ صار لي حادث!
alō, wēnak? ṣār-li ḥādith!
Hello, where are you? I've had an accident!
B
حادث؟! خير؟ شي يعورك؟
ḥādith?! khēr? shay yʿawwrak?
An accident?! Are you OK? Does anything hurt?
A
لا، ما فيني شي، الحمد لله. حادث بسيط
la, ma fīni shay, il-ḥamdu lillāh. ḥādith basīṭ
No, I'm fine, thank God. It's a minor accident.
B
الحمد لله، سلامتك! في أحد تعور؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh, salāmtak! fī aḥad tʿawwar?
Thank God you're OK! Is anyone hurt?
A
الله يسلمك. الريّال الثاني إيده تعورت شوي
allāh ysallmak. ir-rayyāl ith-thāni īdah tʿawwrat shwayy
Thanks. The other man hurt his hand a bit.
B
اتصلت بالإسعاف؟
ittaṣalt bil-isʿāf?
Did you call the ambulance?
A
هيه، والشرطة بعد. الحين ياين
hē, w ish-shurṭa baʿad. il-ḥīn yāyīn
Yes, and the police too. They're on their way now.
items: I'm fine, nothing's wrong with me
to a woman: shay yʿawwrich? (شي يعورج؟)
she got hurt, it got hurt (a feminine thing): tʿawwrat (تعورت); fī aḥad tʿawwar? = is anyone hurt?
did you call the ambulance? (to a man)
to a woman: ittaṣalti bil-isʿāf? (اتصلتي بالإسعاف؟)
